args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. Note: the v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging. Action taken: rolled back checkout-api in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback status: healthy in all regions, error rate 0.2%. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 regression and find out why it was promoted when the staging RC was unhealthy.

trace.final:
checkout-api is rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions and is healthy again. I opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged the on-call engineer.

- **Problem:** The latest release, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** I picked v2.3.0 because it's the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all three regions show healthy and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the follow-up. I checked first and there were no existing incidents.

The release history shows the v2.3.1 test build was already unhealthy in staging before v2.3.1 reached production. I noted this in the incident so someone can look at why it was released anyway.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
